subject: Acme: Integration & model-routing follow-up
messages:
From: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + asks from today's discovery

Thanks again for the call today — great overview. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can validate fit:

- Goal: Reduce latency for customer chat (p95 < 300ms) while keeping token cost under budget for high-volume support flows.
- Current infra: multi-region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on AWS; primary customer traffic in US.
- Key integration needs: Redwood SDK quickstart + auth options, model routing by latency/cost, fallback chains for degraded capacity, structured output for tool-calling (ticket lookup, create), embeddings + reranker for knowledge retrieval.

Asks:
1) Can you send an SDK quickstart pack and sample auth configs (we need to evaluate OIDC + service account options)?
2) Model routing: we want a latency-first policy for chat but cost-aware fallbacks for background tasks. Can you share a proposed policy example?
3) Embeddings & reranker: recommended architecture for a hybrid rerank (ann index + small cross-encoder) and estimated indexing/serve cost.
4) Any infra constraints for region routing or data residency?

Attaching our latest architecture diagram (see link in the drive) — happy to share more if helpful. Procurement is asking for a rough timeline for POC + procurement package.

Thanks,
John Lee
Head of Product, Acme Inc
john.lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T16:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + asks from today's discovery

John — thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the architecture diagram. TL;DR: yes, we can cover all of this in a POC. Attached: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf (quickstart + sample code) and a high-level model-routing-proposal.xlsx with example policies.

Answers / notes:
- SDK & auth: the SDK quickstart in the PDF covers REST/Node/Python snippets. For auth we support API keys, short-lived OIDC service accounts (recommended for multi-region deployments), and HSM/KMS integrations for Private deployments. We'll include rotation recommendations and a sample OIDC config.

- Model routing & policies (high-level):
  - Latency-first policy: route to low-latency instance class (quantized Llama-2 13B variant) in region closest to user; strict p95 guardrails; fallback to regional smaller variant if capacity constrained.
  - Cost-first policy: route to high-throughput, lower-cost quantized model (8-bit) and batch more aggressively for background/async tasks.
  - Fallback chains: primary model -> regional backup -> cross-region fallback (if allowed) -> cached prefix / offline response. The XLSX has example rules and priority weights.

- Region routing: we can set route rules per API key or per-route. For your multi-region needs we recommend: user-facing routes pinned to nearest region + a cross-region fallback policy with data residency flags.

- Structured output / tool calling: Redwood supports function/tool calling with JSON schema enforcement. For ticketing flows we recommend returning a structured payload like:{"action":"create_ticket","fields":{...}} (see SDK doc). We'll provide a sample function definition and validation rules in the quickstart PDF.

- Embeddings & reranker: recommended flow:
  1) Embed docs with our embeddings API and store in your ANN index (we've validated with Faiss/Weaviate).
  2) Retrieve top-K candidates, then run a small cross-encoder (e.g., 2-3B distilled) for re-ranking on the serving cluster.
  3) Cache reranker results for hot queries.
Estimated incremental cost: small compute for cross-encoder per query; spreadsheet has ballpark.

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood: provide more detailed policy examples, sample OIDC config, and an estimate for the POC (owner: me) — deliver by Friday 2/20.
- Acme: confirm which regions you want pinned for user-facing traffic and whether cross-region fallback is allowed (owner: John).
- Technical deep-dive: schedule 60m follow-up next week to walk Dev & Marcus through SDK snippets + routing rules.

I'll schedule the deep-dive once I get your availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + asks from today's discovery

John — quick technical clarifications on auth and structured output options so you can review with your infra team:

Auth options we recommend:
- OIDC service account (short-lived tokens): integrates with your IdP, recommended for multi-region setups. Supports token rotation and per-service scopes.
- API keys: simplest for POC, but not ideal long-term for multi-team access controls.
- Private deployment: customer-managed KMS/HSM + mTLS for control-plane connections.

Sample OIDC config (conceptual):
- issuer: https://accounts.acme.com
- client_id: acme-redwood-svc
- scopes: redwood.read redwood.write
- rotation: 1h token lifetime, 1d refresh window

On structured output & tool-calling: function-calling is supported. Example return contract we recommend for ticket creation flows:
- return JSON with top-level fields: status, action_id, payload.
- include a result_code and validation_errors array for downstream processors.

Model-routing configuration notes (practical):
- Route definitions are per-route and can include: preferred_regions (list), latency_slo_ms (number), cost_budget_cents_per_1k_tokens, fallback_chain (ordered model ids), and re-ranking_flags.
- Example: route.chat.support -> preferred_regions=[us-east,us-west], latency_slo_ms=300, fallback_chain=[redwood-13b-llama-q, redwood-3b-llama-q, cached_response].

Embeddings + reranker ops:
- We recommend batching embedding writes for initial indexing and streaming incremental updates.
- Keep vector index in region-local storage for serving; cross-region replication only if you need global low-latency.

I'll bring a sample route config to the deep-dive. If you want, I can also share a sanitized sample of our policy YAML file ahead of the meeting.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

From: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-17T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + asks from today's discovery

Thanks — couple follow-ups from procurement and infra:

1) Can Redwood enforce per-route cost budgets? Procurement wants a way to cap spend for non-revenue flows.
2) For fallback chains: if primary is down and you route cross-region, do logs / audit trail preserve residency flags? We need to prove to compliance that PII doesn't leave region unless explicitly allowed.
3) Timeline: procurement wants a POC estimate — you mentioned deliverables by 2/20. Can you also provide a simple SOW and checklist for procurement?

On (1): we are thinking of a hard cap per route and alerts at 70/90/100%. Does Redwood support automated throttling or should that be done client-side?

Appreciate the fast turnaround. I'll coordinate with Sara (cc'ed) for procurement.

Regards,
John

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-02-18T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + asks from today's discovery

John / team — quick answers and next steps so procurement has what it needs:

1) Per-route cost budgets: yes — Redwood supports per-route budget settings with alerting thresholds (70/90/100%). We can configure automated throttling and circuit-breakers that will reject or downgrade requests when a budget is hit. For POC, we typically enable alerting + soft-throttle (return 429 with X-RateLimit info) and then move to hard caps if needed.

2) Residency & audit trail: audit logs include the route, model id, serving region, and a residency flag. Cross-region fallback will be explicitly recorded; we can also add an allowlist so fallbacks only occur for routes that permit cross-region. We'll include a sample audit log extract in the SOW.

3) SOW / procurement checklist: I attached a short procurement checklist in the model-routing-proposal.xlsx and will draft a one-page SOW that covers scope (POC: SDK + routing + embeddings/reranker), timeline (2-4 weeks), and deliverables (config templates, integration support, one onsite/remote workshop). I'll have the SOW draft to you by EOD 2/20.

4) Meeting: propose 60m technical deep-dive on 2026-02-24 at 10:00am PT. Please confirm availability so I can send a calendar invite.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf, model-routing-proposal.xlsx
Related links: HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/ACME-001, DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/doc/abc123
